why: Use 'inorder is sorted' as a diagnostic: swapping two values creates one descent (adjacent swap) or two descents in the inorder sequence, and those descents name the two nodes to swap back.
hints: What does the inorder sequence of a valid BST look like? What does swapping two values do to it?

Walk inorder keeping the previous node. At the first descent (prev > cur) the first wrong node is prev; at the last descent the second wrong node is cur. If there is only one descent, both come from it.
Iterative inorder with a stack, then swap the two nodes' values. O(n) time, O(h) space (Morris traversal gives O(1)).
pitfalls: Adjacent swapped values produce only one descent; take both nodes from it.
Swap values, not nodes; the structure must not change.
